text: Revisiting lowers direct broad-group change MSE relative to independent annual samples across the five prespecified budgets.
scope: Thirty fixed test landscapes, three primary2022–2025 contrasts, specified stable agricultural point populations; no national or field-cost inference. Labels are error-free and perfectly repeatable readings of the declaration database; field/photo errors and their temporal dependence are not measured. See review/response-1.md R1-1.
reader_implication: Reference-panel choice materially affects precision, but a relative precision gain alone does not validate reporting. Assess label-error sensitivity before transferring this result to field or photo-interpreted audits.

text: At n=128 the direct revisited intervals have lower aggregate coverage than independent-sample intervals on the main agricultural cohort.
scope: Original delta intervals with gradient floor 1e-6; 20 grassland-dominated and 8 arable-dominated landscapes; aggregate result is qualified by C05. Labels are error-free and perfectly repeatable readings of the declaration database; field/photo errors and their temporal dependence are not measured. See review/response-1.md R1-1.
reader_implication: Test coverage for the intended support and change frequency; do not interpret a nominal level as demonstrated reliability. Assess label-error sensitivity before transferring this result to field or photo-interpreted audits.

text: The no-change point baseline beats n=128 direct and frozen-model-assisted broad estimates in squared error on this cohort.
scope: Main broad-group cohort and original frozen logistic/forest conditions, not the later refreshed or alternative-frame conditions. The point baseline supplies no confidence interval.
reader_implication: Include a simple point baseline when assessing practical precision; its success under MSE does not establish absence of change.

text: The original soft-logistic assisted interval rule, which omitted the projection derivative, gives overly conservative aggregate coverage and rarely reports directions.
scope: Two frozen logistic representations, broad groups, revisited n=128 samples and the original1e-6 floor; not all model-assisted estimators or numerical settings.
reader_implication: This behavior diagnoses the original interval rule, not a general advantage of model assistance; derivative-aware exploratory results are in C11 and review/response-1.md R1-5.

text: The aggregate coverage gap is much smaller on the exploratory complete stable-arable reference frame.
scope: All-year Arable Land support, at least1024pixels, eligible subset of the original landscapes; changes support, composition and signal magnitude together; no causal attribution.
reader_implication: Do not generalize the grassland-inclusive aggregate deficit to every arable crop-diversity application.

text: Revisited draws with no changed labels account for a substantial portion of direct interval misses; the exploratory conservative interval union does not restore nominal coverage.
scope: Exploratory n=128 original broad direct samples; exact ceiling uses known benchmark transition counts; guard is not a uniformly valid replacement interval. Labels are error-free and perfectly repeatable readings of the declaration database; field/photo errors and their temporal dependence are not measured. See review/response-1.md R1-1.
reader_implication: Inspect transition sparsity and zero-standard-error draws before accepting approximate interval reports. Assess label-error sensitivity before transferring this result to field or photo-interpreted audits.

text: Changing only the numerical entropy-gradient floor changes soft-assisted interval coverage and reporting while preserving point estimates exactly.
scope: Exploratory frozen logistic n=128 conditions, floors1e-2through1e-10; no floor selected as operationally calibrated.
reader_implication: Numerical regularization of a boundary derivative must be part of the uncertainty assessment.

text: A coherent half-retained panel has intermediate direct precision and higher simultaneous coverage than the full-revisit panel in this benchmark, without reaching nominal95% joint coverage.
scope: Exploratory coherent2022–2025 samples,128labels/year,30fixed landscapes, tested50%retention only; approximate entropy intervals.
reader_implication: Partial rotation deserves comparison at the intended budget, but this result does not select a universally reliable refresh rate.

text: The prospective native-grid case check exposes differences between sampled-point and whole-population reference changes.
scope: Three cases selected by baseline category/static geometry before target outcomes; no unconditional two-phase coverage estimate or new geography.
reader_implication: A conditional finite-point audit target should not silently be treated as the complete landscape target.

text: The additional stable-arable cohort has an observed broad MSE ratio above 1 and fine ratio below 1; both landscape-resampling ranges include 1.
scope: Exploratory separate geographic cohort, complete stable Arable Land support and the fixed primary period; no independent reproduction, representative national inference or causal rotation effect. Composition sensitivity is unresolved on six landscapes; neither a general reversal nor a fine-taxonomy advantage is established. Interpretation revised after R1-3, review/response-1.md.
reader_implication: A precision gain on broad agricultural support should not be treated as a universal gain for another crop-group support or taxonomy.

text: Applying the local projection derivative changes soft-assisted interval coverage and reporting while preserving all point estimates.
scope: Exploratory original frozen logistic heads at n=128, both hierarchies/representations, locally fixed sampled positive support; support changes and entropy boundaries prevent a general normal-coverage guarantee.
reader_implication: High coverage under the original clipped-gradient rule is not intrinsic evidence of reliable model assistance; specify propagation through the actual transformation.

text: Synthetic independent annual label error reduces the revisited interval coverage deficit while worsening its point accuracy.
scope: Exploratory post-review n=128 broad direct benchmark, fixed error-free target; specified replacement/coupling model, not estimated real error rates or a valid measurement-error interval.
reader_implication: Both repeatability of audit labels and their temporal dependence matter when transferring panel results.

text: Landscape composition sensitivity is wider than Monte Carlo precision of the original fixed-cohort MSE ratio.
scope: Exploratory 5,000 whole-landscape bootstrap resamples of 30 convenience-cohort landscapes, three original contrasts retained per landscape; not national uncertainty.
reader_implication: Separate simulation precision from heterogeneity across landscapes.
